requirement:
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.

The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.

The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. There are no review roots, and none are needed.

I checked each clause for a structural obligation:

- **Eligibility.** The clause is "A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review", plus "A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation other than `habeas:util`". It decides which passages get a review. Any discovery mechanism that produces the same set of reviews satisfies it, so it names no library, algorithm or type.
- **Outermost fence and scope.** The text says "The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage", that nested commentary containers belong to the same review, and that nested requirement or example declarations belong to their own assessments. These rules say which citations belong to which review. A different parser or traversal gives the same grouping, so they are behavioral.
- **Subject and inputs.** The text says "The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather than the whole chapter", and that inputs include the passage and each cited declaration or built-in text. These are observable contents of the review record and prompt. They do not prescribe a signature, type or field layout.
- **Judgment criteria.** These are "the passage's claims agree with and are supported by the cited declarations" and "Contradicting or unsupported claims produce a negative assessment". Built-in citations "retain their permitted-role and stated-criteria checks". These describe how the reviewer judges, which is behavior, not code structure.
- **Reuse of the existing workflow.** The text says "These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection, and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`". It also says identities follow the outline-selector rules and rendering follows {cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. An implementation could keep a separate code path that writes the same `evidence/citations/...` records with the same staleness, selection and rendering behavior. That would look identical from outside, so the code-sharing is discretionary. The storage, freshness and selection obligations are enforced by `requirements.references.citation_review`, which is cited for context. The rendering obligations are enforced by `requirements.references.book_badges`, which is also cited. This requirement does not add its own structural duty.
- **Unfenced citations.** "Unfenced book citations retain their existing behavior" is a behavioral constraint.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation of `requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.

**Opt-in and eligibility**
- `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_groups_nested_citations_but_excludes_declarations_and_literals]` builds a chapter with many cases and asserts that exactly one book item results from `md/notes.md`. Its exact citation list is `habeas:util`, `requirements.ready`, `requirements.ready`, `notes.nested`, `notes.illustration` and `habeas:coverage`. That list rules out each of these:
  - the unfenced inline citation;
  - the `habeas:util`-only fence;
  - the fence citing the unresolved `requirements.missing`;
  - the unclosed fence;
  - a cite fence inside a `{req}` declaration;
  - a fenced code literal;
  - an escaped role.
- It also asserts that the same fence in a source file outside the book (`notes.md`) is `ReviewKind::SourceItem`, while the book one is `ReviewKind::BookCommentary`.
- A `habeas:util` opening fence that holds other resolved citations is itself the outermost passage, so the "other than `habeas:util`" rule is exercised in both directions.
- `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[separate_closed_passages_have_independent_subjects_and_empty_book_cites_stay_exempt]` checks that two separate closed fences give two items. It also checks that a fence inside HTML is a literal and is ignored. It checks that an inline-only citation in a book chapter creates no review, which is the "unfenced citations retain existing behavior" rule.

**Outermost fence, nesting, and the subject outline node**
- In the grouping test, the nested `{cite}` fence and the citations in the body are grouped into one review. The nested `{req}` and `{example}` citations are excluded.
- The test resolves the item's outline node and asserts that its text starts with `:::::{cite} habeas:util`. It asserts that the text contains the outer and nested passage text but not the unfenced chapter text or the utility-only passage.
- This shows that the subject is the enclosing citation fence node, not the chapter.

**Identities**
- The separate-passages test asserts that the items and their `review_path()` values differ.
- The batch test uses the outline-selector-based `evidence_path`.

**Inputs, prompt, and assessment**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_reviews_supply_the_whole_passage_and_check_concordance]` asserts that the mandatory inputs include these, with the passage node first:
  - the passage's file and item;
  - the built-in `habeas:coverage` text;
  - `requirements.ready`;
  - the definition `terms.unit` that the cited requirement uses.
- It asserts that the prompt has "Review kind: book_commentary", the passage text, the cited declaration and the definition text. It also asserts "Contradicting or unsupported claims are gaps" and that there is no surrounding chapter text.
- It records an assessment with the correct file and item.
- A changed passage is reassessed, and a false determination is recorded. `validate_review` then reports "determination is false", so a contradicting claim gives a negative review.
- Built-in role and criteria checks stay under `requirements.references.citation_review`. That requirement is cited, not restated here.

**Storage, freshness, selection, `author --all`, and orphans**
- The assessment test asserts that a changed passage makes the review stale (a "hash" error).
- It asserts that removing the fence gives an "orphaned citation review" error.
- `src/authoring/batch.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_passages_are_selected_refreshed_skipped_and_removed_with_citation_reviews]` covers these book-passage cases:
  - a missing review is selected;
  - a current review is skipped, with `unchanged == 1`;
  - `--all` forces a refresh;
  - an edited passage is reselected;
  - an orphaned review is deleted.

**Delegated**
- Rendering is delegated to `requirements.references.book_badges` and the display requirement.
- Detailed storage and freshness rules belong to `requirements.references.citation_review`.
- These are cited, not restated here.

I found no behavioral obligation without a test and no marking gap.

A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} book_badges
In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline
or fenced, renders as a Shields.io static badge image, subject to the
citation-only paragraph exception below and the reviewed-passage display under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary.display`.
The badge has meaningful alt text displaying its role and full name, and links
to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links
work across chapters, including nested chapters. Apart from the reviewed-passage
exception, a fenced reference renders its badge followed by its body as Markdown.
Inside any prose-bearing colon-fenced section, top-level paragraphs containing
one or more valid inline `{cite}` references and otherwise only whitespace are
omitted from the chapter. This applies to requirements, examples, definitions,
reference fences, and other prose containers, including nested sections.
Requirement and example detail pages still render those citations.
Citations within explanatory prose, lists or blockquotes, unfenced chapter
prose, and references of other roles retain their usual rendering.
Escaped roles, code, raw HTML, and unresolvable references remain literal.
The original declaration, reference discovery, and authoring inputs retain the
citations.
Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive renders with a badge identifying
its kind and full name; text outside a directive remains literal. Declaration
badge navigation follows {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`.
Badge text remains legible regardless of whether its link has been visited.
A badge link shows a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and may
brighten on hover. Badges may be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a
fenced reference's badge and body may be visually set apart from the surrounding
text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge may show a help cursor to
signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
